title: Create green-season demand with MICE and events

blocks.text: Theme 1.1 · Traveller, brand and proposition · Focus area 2
Create green-season demand with MICE and events

The green season is a seat problem and an events problem at once. June holds 6.4% of the year's international seats, and business events are the lever best placed to fill the trough, though international meetings now peak from September to November.

**December 2025.** Develop the Seasonality and Spread Proposition (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p64), reprinted from March 2026 as Develop seasonality, spread and Mega events proposition (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p7).

**October 2026: Reworded.** June holds 6.4% of seats, and ICCA meetings cluster from May to November. Spread moved to focus areas 3 and 10, and business events replaced mega events as the lever. MIDAS's seasonality analysis and the Demand-Side MICE landscape drove the change.
Seats and visitors both fall away from April to September. Business events do not.

blocks.text: Two limits matter. The October to March share is about 62% for 2025, computed from a month-of-travel table whose shares sum to 104.9% and normalised (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p12). The only printed split is 61% to 39% for 2024 (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p32), and the report carries both. And only conferences are measured: meetings are absent from provincial statistics, incentive volumes are unverified and exhibitions are unquantified (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p36).

Wesgro should build an April to September events spine and sell it with the seats. The Diagnostic proposed the spine itself, anchored on a small set of flagship weeks, with green-season flight, stay and experience packages sold through airline and trade partners (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p32). The Demand-Side Analysis adds the routes by segment: off-peak conference bids in sectors where the province is strong, cooler-season incentive packages for Indian and Gulf planners, and winter midweek packages for corporate meetings (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p40).

rows: Publish a green-season events calendar and aim Convention Bureau bids at May to September in the province's strongest sectors
Package green-season flight, stay and experiences with airlines and trade, and test cooler-season incentive packages with Indian and Gulf planners
Measure meetings, incentives and exhibitions, which provincial statistics do not cover today
Programme lifestyle events in December and January and keep peak dates for international events; market flower, fynbos and whale events earlier
CTICC; Overberg and West Coast LTOs
Agree one event acquisition and calendar strategy across Wesgro, the Convention Bureau, the City and the Province
Ease visas for regional African delegates, whose event demand the venue operator rates as visa-constrained
Home Affairs; SA National Convention Bureau

blocks.text: Victoria curates a portfolio of global, cultural, regional and business events that generate repeat, predictable demand spikes across the year, and Melbourne's monthly arrivals stay between 7% and 12% of the year (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p17, p18). The required change for the Western Cape is a unified event acquisition and calendar strategy across Wesgro, the Convention Bureau, the City and the Province, with a proactive conference bidding pipeline (p20).

**Initiative I2**, green-season events and business-events calendar (section 4.3). **Indicators** T1-05 green-season share at impact level, and T2-02 ICCA meetings and T2-03 April to September seat share at outcome level (section 5.2).
